purpose: Three-replicate stochastic robustness analysis on a prespecified, scientifically stratified subset of the 30-case benchmark.
vertex_project_handling: Read at execution time from the authorized local Google Cloud configuration; never commit the project identifier.

legacy_replicate_1_policy.disclosure: Legacy replicate 1 lacks an embedded run-specific code hash and exact API token metadata; reuse is limited to outputs that passed the observable topic, cutoff, model, temperature, prompt/code, rounds, and frozen-evidence audit.

primary_criteria: Stratify across solid-state, lithium-ion, sodium-ion, potassium-ion, aqueous zinc-ion, and lithium-selenium systems.
Include both reviewer-identified high-leakage prompts and lower-leakage controls.
Include the protocol-centered case 29 to reduce dependence on particle-morphology tasks.
Cover cathode, anode, architecture, composition, transport, confinement, and testing-protocol reasoning.
selection_rule.legacy_score_use: Legacy IHQ scores were not a primary inclusion rule. They were checked only after scientific stratification to confirm that the subset was not composed solely of favorable MPDS outcomes.

cases.stratum: solid-state cathode / manuscript Case Study 2 / very-high leakage
cases.reason: Directly addresses the reviewer-raised Case Study 2 consistency and prompt-leakage concerns.
Anchors the second manuscript case study and the electrolyte/interphase blind-spot discussion.

cases.stratum: lithium-ion oxide anode / process-density trade-off / EOP repair
cases.reason: Represents oxide microsphere design and provides a direct validation case for the corrected EOP pipeline.
Adds a cathode-side multivalent-ion transport problem outside the dominant Li/Na anode group.
The reviewer explicitly identified its hollow-sulfide/rGO wording as answer-revealing.
Introduces shuttle suppression, selenium confinement, and electrolyte-access trade-offs.
Tests generalization to large-ion transport and severe alloying/conversion volume change.

cases.stratum: lithium-ion anode / one-dimensional architecture / very-high leakage
cases.reason: Provides a second, structurally distinct high-leakage stress test through the tube-in-tube clue.
The only protocol-centered task, reducing dependence on morphology-generation questions.
Adds a 2024 cutoff and a composition-versus-inactive-mass/transport trade-off.
